parsed.explanation: The combined regime is a military junta's new penal code (in force 13 Dec 2024) criminalising same-sex conduct at 2–5 years' imprisonment, keyed to sex assigned at birth — so a trans visitor's relationship and even perceived conduct fall squarely inside it. Since enactment, arbitrary arrests, detentions and physical abuse based on appearance or gender expression alone have significantly increased: state-tolerated targeting against visibly gender-nonconforming people. Pre-existing Article 225 morality provisions were already used against GNC expression, showing the enforcement pattern the new law inherits. No anti-discrimination law, no complaint body, a 98%-hostile society, and junta repression leave no realistic recourse. No execution or custody-torture record keeps this just above the 0.15 tier.

entry_documents.exposure: No visitor-specific entry rule documented, but offence fixed by sex assigned at birth means any discovered relationship or presentation can trigger prosecution; mismatched presentation alone has driven arrests since Dec 2024.
entry_documents.interaction: Outing at any checkpoint or encounter converts presentation into a criminal matter under the nationwide code.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Significant documented increase in arbitrary arrests and detentions since the code took effect, including on appearance/gender expression alone; imprisonment carries 2–5 years plus fine.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No count, review mechanism, or bail record is given.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor stopped for any reason enters the same nationwide arrest pattern; junta security apparatus controls custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Nationwide penal code with no subnational variation; prison placement practice for trans detainees is explicitly not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Arrest under the national code leads into an undocumented but unreformed custodial system with no identity protections on record.

care_services.exposure: No documented trans-specific care access rule or emergency-care protection; hostility extends to health settings through general anti-LGBT climate.
care_services.interaction: Medical contact after arrest or injury would occur within a system offering no recognition of affirmed gender.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The junta justified the code as defending traditional moral values; the justice minister pledged criminalisation, calling homosexuality unnatural. Vague 'promotion' ban reaches anyone encouraging it, undefined and expansive.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing licenses police and public action against visibly gender-nonconforming visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: A travelling parent accompanied by a minor faces the same birth-sex-keyed criminalisation; presentation-based abuse reaches the family unit, and no family-protection or custody safeguard for trans visitors is documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Presence of a minor adds exposure to moral-panic framing under the regime's values-defence rationale.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented increase in physical abuse based on appearance or gender expression alone since Dec 2024; significant societal stigma (98% disapproval figure, 2007, addressing homosexuality); historical use of morality laws against GNC expression.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented. No anti-discrimination law, no protection body, no LGBT organisations with legal footing.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are perpetrators or bystanders; a visitor has no domestic complaint mechanism to invoke.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law, no protection body, association law impedes advocacy, junta clamps on opposition and media. Recourse is effectively absent.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Scale of new arrests is qualitative only; prison placement, entry screening and trans-specific tolerance remain unresolved unknowns, but absence of data in a repressive state is not safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.15-B, this jurisdiction detains visitors after document/presentation discrepancy under an immigration-adjacent morality regime with ill-treatment and failing courts. It sits slightly higher only because custody violence, medical denial and capital references are not documented here — but the criminalisation, the presentation-based arrests and the absence of remedy are structurally the same tier.

Far below 0.35-B: there, detention 'rarely becomes imprisonment' and courts formally accept complaints. Here imprisonment of 2–5 years is the statutory outcome, arrests for presentation alone are increasing, physical abuse is documented, and no complaint mechanism exists. 0.35 describes exclusion and humiliation; this dossier describes criminal liability and state-tolerated abuse.

Below 0.25-D: there, police act selectively under a vague morality clause but appellate judges annul cases, pleas are available, and penalties are fines and short jail terms. Here a nationwide post-junta code carries 2–5 years, arrests are rising qualitatively, and no functioning appellate restraint or rights body is documented.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is one system: a junta-promulgated penal code keyed to birth sex criminalises any relationship or perceived conduct of a visibly trans visitor at 2–5 years, while the pre-existing morality provisions that already targeted gender-nonconforming expression show the enforcement template. Since 13 December 2024, arrests, detention and physical abuse on appearance alone have significantly increased — state-tolerated targeting, not scattered crime. Official framing (minister's pledges, 'traditional values' justification) and a 98%-hostile societal baseline align law and society against the traveller. No anti-discrimination statute, no protection body, no LGBT association footing and suppressed media leave zero recourse. Unknowns (custody placement, entry screening) are unresolved in a thin-data repressive state and cannot be read as safety; extrapolating from the criminalisation regime and governance character, they likely worsen the picture.
